A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SEREP and MultiREX. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and sufficiently complete to match retained material and identify revisions.

before.justification: V1 reports original expression-reconstruction, identity-preservation and MultiREX experiments in Tables 1–3, alongside qualitative capture and retargeting results.

after.justification: V3 retains these original experiments and adds component ablations, challenging-condition examples and inference-time measurements.

M1.justification: The reported reconstruction-loss weight changes from 0.001 in v1 Appendix A.1 to 1.0 in v3 Appendix A, revising the specified objective weighting. Architecture and component losses otherwise remain unchanged. The three-stage overview reorganizes the existing pipeline; the PDFs do not establish whether the weight revision reflects retraining or a documentation correction.

E1.justification: V3 adds explicit qualitative testing under challenging lighting, external occlusion and motion blur in Appendix D.3 and Figure 16. Training datasets, the representation test set, MultiREX subjects and viewpoints, and the principal capture/retargeting tasks remain unchanged.

E2.justification: TEASER is added to the main in-the-wild retargeting comparison in v3 Section 5.4 and Figure 7, alongside DECA, EMICA, SMIRK and 3DDFA-V3. The FLAME representation comparison and DECA/EMICA/SMIRK MultiREX comparator set are retained. MonoNPHM is newly discussed but not evaluated.

E3.justification: V3 introduces controlled loss-removal and decoder-conditioning experiments and a timing protocol using batch size one on a 2080Ti, excluding bounding-box detection. It also revises the reported reconstruction-loss weight from 0.001 to 1.0 without establishing reruns. The retained benchmark sample counts, alignment procedures and metrics are unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's existing synthetic-only comparison and viewpoint analysis, v3 adds ablations of delta regularization, decoder identity conditioning, domain loss, eye-closure loss and edge preservation (Sections 4.4 and 5.5; Appendix C). Appendix D.3 adds challenging-condition and failure analysis. These substantially expand testing of the method's central components and robustness.

E5.justification: Both versions use the same mean-plus/minus reporting and Wilcoxon signed-rank significance criterion of 0.001. V3 extends these practices to additional result rows without introducing seed counts, repeated-training-run information, confidence intervals or a different uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Retained entries in Tables 1–3 are numerically unchanged, but v3 adds substantive findings. Without delta regularization, reconstruction error is 1.75 mm; without decoder identity conditioning, CSIM is 0.773 versus 0.791 for the full model. Without domain loss, MultiREX error is 2.10 versus 2.19 mm. New qualitative comparisons, failure examples and 26.1 ms inference timing further extend the results.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulations and loss definitions are retained, apart from notation and term ordering. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs that are added or revised in v3; the loss-weight revision is a training specification.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain semantic identity/expression separation, semi-supervised monocular capture, identity-preserving retargeting and MultiREX. V3 foregrounds the identity-aware decoder and inexpensive synthetic data, but these capabilities and their claimed advantages were already present in v1.

C2.justification: V3 substantially expands the explanation of component roles and applicability boundaries. It interprets decoder-conditioning and delta-loss ablations, explicitly identifies a tradeoff between domain loss's worse MultiREX error and qualitatively better in-the-wild generalization, and acknowledges the lack of quantitative unconstrained evaluation. Appendix D.3 additionally identifies motion-blur-induced jitter and dependence on landmark-detector quality.

D1.justification: V3 replaces MultiREX's 'Coming soon' placeholder with a repository link, adds a project-page pointer, and reports hardware, batch size and component-level inference timings. Architecture Tables 4–5 are retained, although some v1 prose specifying graph pooling, upsampling and encoder–decoder skip connections is omitted.

R1.justification: V3 adds discussion or citations for MonoNPHM, local anatomically constrained facial performance retargeting and TEASER, while removing several general representation-learning, disentanglement and capture-background references. The principal positioning against linear 3DMMs, paired expression models and expensive realistic synthetic training remains.

P1.justification: The introduction and conclusion are extensively rewritten, the method narrative explicitly separates three stages, and experimental-procedure explanations are consolidated. The appendices are reorganized from A.1–A.4 into sections A–F, with additional subsections and acknowledgements. This is substantial narrative restructuring beyond inserting new results.

P2.justification: V3 replaces Figure 2 with a three-stage pipeline overview, redraws Figure 4, expands Tables 1–2 and adds a TEASER column to the main qualitative comparison. New Figures 5, 8, 10 and 16 display ablations and challenging cases. Existing benchmark, mask and synthetic-sample figures are retained but redistributed.

improvement.justification: V3 addresses v1's limited component-level validation with direct tests of identity conditioning and the principal losses, substantially strengthening assessment of the central design choices. Reporting the unfavorable MultiREX domain-loss result, failure conditions and runtime also improves transparency. Headline scores remain unchanged, and the unexplained reconstruction-weight revision and qualitative-only in-the-wild generalization evidence remain limitations, but the added controls materially improve the paper's empirical support.
